title: fix(update): keep the failure that started recovery in failure reports
body:
Related: #197083

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: update failure reports drop the step that actually failed when the recovery steps that follow it also fail.

## User Impact

User impact: when an update fails and its recovery also fails, the failure report and triage prompt now include the step that started the problem, so users can report it and maintainers can diagnose it. Reports written by already-installed updaters are unchanged; this applies once a release containing it drives the update.

## Why This Change Was Made

After any post-install failure, the recovery steps that follow (for example `gateway migration recovery`, `package-backup-retention`, `gateway recovery verification`) record their own failures. The report sanitizer kept only the latest three failed steps and pruned the oldest first under its byte budget, so the triggering failure was always the record removed. On #197083 the reporter's report shows exactly this: three recovery failures, `omittedDetails: 2`, and no trace of what started recovery.

The sanitizer now keeps the first failed step alongside the latest two. When the byte budget forces pruning, it protects the first and latest failures by identity, removes other records first (including lint inventory records that follow the latest failure), and drops the first failure before the latest one when only those two remain.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/commands/triage-update.test.ts`: a #197083-shaped record keeps `database rollback` plus the two latest recovery failures; prompt-budget pruning keeps the trigger and the latest failure; artifact-budget pruning with a trailing lint record keeps both failures. The first two fail on base; the trailing-lint test fails on the first PR head and passes now. The existing bounded-evidence test and the recovery prompt test in `src/commands/triage-recovery.test.ts` now expect the first failure.
- All 13 test files that consume the failure sanitizer pass locally (run on head `1b3452f44ad`).
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files clean; `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass; test-line ratchet OK (+107).
- autoreview (P2): scoped-clean on `1b3452f44ad`. Independent `codex exec` review: an earlier round found a P2 (a trailing lint record made pruning drop the latest failure), fixed in `1b3452f44ad`; the final round on `1b3452f44ad` found nothing.
- First CI run (on `66bb77435c3`): `triage-recovery.test.ts` failed from this change (fixed above); `pr-wrapper-source-closure` hit a 120 s timeout in unrelated tooling; one shard hit the runner's daily sandbox-start quota.
- Source check of the released 2026.10.9 updater: `gateway migration recovery` runs only after a refused database rollback (`state-migrated-no-rollback`), so a triggering failure always precedes it.
